subject: Calculating area, kurtosis, skewness of ggplot

messages.author: 159ac5a66c80c1d5
messages.subject: Calculating area, kurtosis, skewness of ggplot
parts:
Dear all,

apologies if these are obvious questions but I am new to the wonders
of R...

I have the following plot:

ggplot(histogrameg, aes(log(Total_scale+1), fill=Typepara)) +
geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +xlab("Log (Total study scale+1)") +ylab("%
of studies")

which basically produces two bell-shaped(ish) curves (Typepara==A and
B) that nicely overlap in the middle.

1) I understand that the area of these graphs will be 1 (as it is
using geom_density) - is this correct?

2) I would like to know how to calculate the overall skewness +
kurtosis of these graphs so I have some numbers to actually describe
the shapes that have been produced - how can I do this?

I also have the another plot:

ggplot(histogrameg, aes(log(Total_scale+1), fill=Parameter)) +
geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +xlab("Log (Total study scale+1)") +ylab("%
of studies")

here there are 11 different "Parameter" (each is either labelled Type
"A" or "B").

3) any ideas how I may produce two plots, one which plots only those
parameters labelled "A" and those "B" in my data?

Many thanks for the help in advance.

On Mon, Mar 14, 2011 at 10:54, afj <johnson.andr...@googlemail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

apologies if these are obvious questions but I am new to the wonders
of R...

I have the following plot:

ggplot(histogrameg, aes(log(Total_scale+1), fill=Typepara)) +
geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +xlab("Log (Total study scale+1)") +ylab("%
of studies")

which basically produces two bell-shaped(ish) curves (Typepara==A and
B) that nicely overlap in the middle.

1) I understand that the area of these graphs will be 1 (as it is
using geom_density) - is this correct?

2) I would like to know how to calculate the overall skewness +
kurtosis of these graphs so I have some numbers to actually describe
the shapes that have been produced - how can I do this?

This will need to be computed outside of ggplot AFAIK, google "R kurtosis" or "R Skewness" for functions that can do this.  If you need/want to add these values to the graph you will probably end up using geom_text().

I also have the another plot:

  ggplot(histogrameg, aes(log(Total_scale+1), fill=Parameter)) +
geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +xlab("Log (Total study scale+1)") +ylab("%
of studies")

here there are 11 different "Parameter" (each is either labelled Type
"A" or "B").

3) any ideas how I may produce two plots, one which plots only those
parameters labelled "A" and those "B" in my data?
I would suggest faceting.

ggplot(histogrameg, aes(log(Total_scale+1), fill=Parameter)) +
geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +xlab("Log (Total study scale+1)") +ylab("%
of studies") + facet_grid(~Typepara)
Many thanks for the help in advance.
